neural networks, in the presence of a large amount of variables and when a set of variables is chosen by a criterion adapted to the network, can lead to more accurate results than traditional statistical methods, and that this is due to the ability of neural networks to find complex relationships between the variables.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of the variable selection technique has a significant influence on the prediction accuracy of the model and on its structure.
the use of a set of variables chosen with a criterion adapted to the classification method used leads to a more accurate model than the use of sets chosen with criteria used by financial analysts.

a neural network model using a set chosen with the criterion of the best representation of healthy companies leads to a more accurate classification than a model using a set selected with the criterion of maximum information content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a set of variables adapted to the structure of the model is essential to obtain accurate results in bankruptcy prediction.

, when the objective is to design models that predict the financial failure of a company, the selection of variables must be made with the objective of minimizing the number of errors of type I, and that the structure of a neural network model is an important element in achieving this objective.
the selection of a classification method should be based on the characteristics of the data set.
